description: For every DIRECT_CAUSATION edge, the class of study anchoring it, in three tiers. FLAGGED (associationOrPrevalenceOnly): no causal-capable anchor anywhere on the edge and at least one anchor states a prevalence or association finding. DESCRIPTIVE_ANCHOR (mechanismAssertedBySecondaryOnly): the causal step is named only inside a review, guideline, consensus or case report, with no primary analytic study anywhere on the edge. PRIMARY_ANCHORED: at least one anchor is a longitudinal/prospective/incidence design, a randomised trial, or a Mendelian-randomisation design. Verdicts for the flagged and descriptive-anchor rows are authored in docs/dc-anchor-audit-2026-10-06.md.

lexicon.label: PREVALENCE_OR_ASSOCIATION
lexicon.note: Reports frequency, co-occurrence, correlation, or a population-level risk/odds association.

lexicon.label: ANALYTIC_LONGITUDINAL
lexicon.note: Temporal ordering: prospective, longitudinal, incidence, or a cohort with follow-up. A bare 'cohort' is deliberately NOT enough — a cross-sectional cohort is a prevalence design.

lexicon.label: DESCRIPTIVE_SOURCE
lexicon.note: A review, guideline, consensus, editorial, chapter, case report or case series: it can state a mechanism, but it does not itself measure a causal step.

lexicon.label: RANDOMIZED
lexicon.note: Randomised allocation: a trial, or a review restricted to trials.

lexicon.label: CAUSAL_INFERENCE_DESIGN
lexicon.note: Randomisation by nature: Mendelian randomisation, instrumental variables.

lexicon.label: MECHANISM
lexicon.note: Describes the pathophysiological or physical step itself, not its frequency.

lexicon.label: INTERVENTION_RESPONSE
lexicon.note: The anchor measures a change produced by an intervention rather than a frequency.

references.citation: Litta F et al. Tech Coloproctol. 2021;25(4):385-399. PMID 33387100
references.note: Systematic review of 66 studies reported postoperative continence impairment in 12.7% of patients undergoing sphincter-cutting treatment for simple anal fistula; study quality was generally low. Supports a procedure-specific continence-complication pathway, not automatic attribution from the fistula diagnosis itself.

references.citation: Moradi et al., BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders (2025), PMID 40380123
references.note: Systematic review of 20 studies focused on surgically treated lumbar disc herniation/CES populations; persistent sexual dysfunction was common after CES and erectile dysfunction was the most frequently reported male sexual disorder. Supports this bounded postoperative population, not unrestricted generalization across all CES etiologies or automatic individual causation.

references.citation: Fallo et al., Diagnosis and management of hypertension in patients with Cushing's syndrome: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension, J Hypertens. 2022;40(11):2085-2101. PMID 35950979
references.note: Endocrine-hypertension consensus states that hypertension is common in Cushing's syndrome and may persist after normalization of hormone excess or steroid withdrawal; supports a disease-specific endocrine hypertension pathway with individual diagnosis and chronology safeguards.

references.citation: Ocampo-Navia MI, Perez-Mendez W, Rodriguez-Alvarez MP, Chadid-Contreras J, Vergara MF. Dandy-Walker syndrome: an updated literature review. Childs Nerv Syst. 2025;41(1):194. PMID 40445443. doi:10.1007/s00381-025-06842-0.
references.note: Updated review: DWS occurs in 1 in 25,000-35,000 live births and often presents with hydrocephalus and other CNS anomalies; management involves treating hydrocephalus, and prognosis hinges on associated malformations.

references.citation: Spennato P, Mirone G, Nastro A, Buonocore MC, Ruggiero C, Trischitta V, Aliberti F, Cinalli G. Hydrocephalus in Dandy-Walker malformation. Childs Nerv Syst. 2011;27(10):1665-1681. PMID 21928031. doi:10.1007/s00381-011-1544-4.
references.note: Definitive review dedicated to the hydrocephalus-DWM relationship: therapeutic control of hydrocephalus (single shunting of ventricle or cyst, or endoscopic third ventriculostomy) is effective, and prognosis and intellectual outcome depend on associated malformations and the adequate control of hydrocephalus.

references.citation: Bokhari I, Rehman L, Hassan S, Hashim MS. Dandy-Walker Malformation: A Clinical and Surgical Outcome Analysis. J Coll Physicians Surg Pak. 2015;25(6):431-433. PMID 26100996.
references.note: Surgical case series (n=70): hydrocephalus was present in all patients as the predominant presenting feature; shunt malfunction and infection were the commonest post-treatment complications.

references.citation: Catarina Oliveira A, Figueiredo R, Correia R, et al. Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease: A contemporary case series from a large university hospital. Nefrologia (Engl Ed). 2026;46(7):501522. PMID 42618193.
references.note: Contemporary case series documenting 92.6% renal replacement requirement at presentation, crescentic glomerulonephritis in 80% of biopsies, and limited renal recovery (18.5% of those presenting on renal replacement) with crescent burden above 40% and absent preserved glomeruli predicting poor outcome despite therapy - the renal-destruction and non-recovery anchor.

references.citation: Suhlrie A, van der Meijden WAG, Faguer S, et al. Outcomes in Children and Adults With Antiglomerular Basement Membrane Disease. Kidney Int Rep. 2026;11(5):106353. PMID 42006224.
references.note: Cohort of 72 children and adults with anti-GBM disease documenting rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with dialysis at diagnosis a strong predictor of outcome regardless of age under plasma-exchange-based treatment - the dialysis-outcome predictor anchor.

references.citation: Wang Y, Zhai Z, Wang L, et al. Rituximab is associated with accelerated dialysis independence in anti-glomerular basement membrane disease: a multicenter retrospective study. Front Immunol. 2026;17:1835889. PMID 42199438.
references.note: Multicenter study of 66 confirmed anti-GBM patients documenting dialysis independence in about half recovering, accelerated dialysis independence with rituximab addition, and a trend toward higher renal survival with initial dialysis dependency a predictor - the subset-recovery and treatment-response anchor that grounds the PROBABLE (not WELL_ESTABLISHED) ceiling.

references.citation: Barritt AS 4th, Qasim A, Kim Y, Miller SD, O'Donnell J, Johnston K. Prognostic value of liver histology in steatotic liver disease: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis. J Comp Eff Res. 2026 Sep 3:e260148. doi:10.57264/cer-2026-0148. PMID 42690133.
references.note: Systematic literature review and meta-analysis pooling 32 studies of histologic liver fibrosis in steatotic liver disease showing that higher fibrosis stage is associated with increasing risk of major adverse liver outcomes including cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma - the meta-analytic natural-history anchor for a probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Wang X, Dong X, Qian L, Yang Z, Yang D, Niu Y. Non-invasive Tests for the Prediction of Liver-related Events in Patients with MASLD: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Radiol. 2026 Jul 22:S1076-6332(26)00476-9. doi:10.1016/j.acra.2026.06.068. PMID 42481370.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of non-invasive tests for the prediction of liver-related events in MASLD, documenting the progression of metabolic steatotic liver disease to cirrhosis and its complications - the independent corroboration anchor for the fibrosing-progression pathway.

references.citation: Jones et al., 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults, Circulation. 2025;152(11):e114-e218. PMID 40811497
references.note: Current multidisciplinary guideline identifies high blood pressure as a modifiable risk factor for development of chronic kidney disease and provides CKD-specific hypertension management recommendations; supports a target-organ-damage research pathway while requiring individual renal etiology and chronology review.

references.citation: Jones et al., 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults, Circulation. 2025;152(11):e114-e218. PMID 40811497
references.note: Current guideline's heart-failure-prevention section describes antecedent hypertension, a dose-dependent BP-heart-failure association, and reduced heart-failure risk with long-term blood-pressure treatment; supports a hypertension-to-heart-failure progression pathway with individual etiology safeguards.

references.citation: Stevens DL, Bryant AE. Streptococcus pyogenes Impetigo, Erysipelas, and Cellulitis. In: Ferretti JJ, Stevens DL, Fischetti VA, editors. Streptococcus pyogenes: Basic Biology to Clinical Manifestations [Internet]. 2nd edition. Oklahoma City (OK): University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center; 2022 Oct 8. Chapter 23. PMID 36479753.
references.note: Reference chapter on group A streptococcal skin and soft-tissue infection stating that impetigo is a non-life-threatening infection but can result in post-streptococcal acute glomerulonephritis - the disease-specific complication statement anchoring the impetigo-to-nephritis proposition.

references.citation: Ilyas M, Tolaymat A. Changing epidemiology of acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis in Northeast Florida: a comparative study. Pediatr Nephrol. 2008 Jul;23(7):1101-1106. doi:10.1007/s00467-008-0778-1. PMID 18373105.
references.note: Comparative epidemiological study of paediatric acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis in which 66% of the earlier cohort had antecedent pyoderma (versus a recent cohort predominantly pharyngitis-associated) - the cohort-level antecedent-skin-infection anchor and the basis for the recorded era and population caveat.

references.citation: Garbarino et al., Behavioral Sleep Medicine (2020), PMID 30453780
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis found anxiety symptoms common in adults with OSA and described the relationship among OSA, anxiety, and depression as probably bidirectional; supports association, not automatic individual causation.

references.citation: Bandak M, Jørgensen N, Juul A, et al. Testosterone deficiency in testicular cancer survivors - a systematic review and meta-analysis. Andrology. 2016;4(3):382-388. PMID 27009402
references.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 12 publications found increased testosterone-deficiency risk after standard chemotherapy (OR 1.8), non-conventional therapy (OR 3.1), and infradiaphragmatic radiotherapy (OR 1.6) compared with testicular germ-cell cancer survivors treated with orchiectomy alone. Supports a treatment-specific hypogonadism pathway, not automatic attribution from the cancer diagnosis itself.

references.citation: Scheffel TB, Diz FM, Wieck A, Begnini KR, da Costa JC. The molecular landscape of glioblastoma-associated epilepsy. J Mol Med (Berl). 2025;103(8):923-933. PMID 40576825. doi:10.1007/s00109-025-02567-4.
references.note: Review of glioblastoma-associated epilepsy documenting seizures as a common symptom reflecting tumor microenvironment interactions, with molecular mechanisms including increased glutamate release, ion-channel dysfunction, inflammation, and shared synaptic and immune pathways; supports the direct tumor-driven seizure mechanism, not a statistical comorbidity framing.

references.citation: Kerkhof M, Benit C, Duran-Pena A, Vecht CJ. Seizures in oligodendroglial tumors. CNS Oncol. 2015;4(5):347-356. PMID 26478444. doi:10.2217/cns.15.29.
references.note: Review reporting epilepsy development in more than 70 to 90 percent of oligodendroglial tumors with glutamate and GABA metabolism alterations implicated in glioma-associated epilepsy and seizure outcomes after surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy; supports the tumor-driven seizure physiology within the glial-tumor spectrum, not individual claim determination.

references.citation: Chinese Society of Hepatology et al., Consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of hepatic fibrosis (2019), J Dig Dis. 2020;21:127-138. PMID 32108989
references.note: Evidence-based consensus describing hepatic fibrosis as a key developmental step across chronic liver diseases leading to cirrhosis; supports a fibrosis-progression pathway, not an automatic individual nexus.

references.citation: Leslie SW, Aeddula NR. Vesicoureteral Reflux. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing; updated 2024 Apr 30. PMID 33085409.
references.note: StatPearls review: neurogenic bladder is a recognized cause of vesicoureteral reflux, and high-pressure bladder conditions are key predictors of additional renal damage and scarring; reflux nephropathy accounts for about 5% of pediatric renal transplants.

references.citation: Wu CQ, Franco I. Management of vesicoureteral reflux in neurogenic bladder. Investig Clin Urol. 2017;58(Suppl 1):S54-S58. PMID 28612061. doi:10.4111/icu.2017.58.S1.S54.
references.note: Review: VUR in neurogenic bladder develops through a defective ureterovesical junction or an overwhelmed normal UVJ mechanism caused by bladder dysfunction; VUR is a significant risk factor for pyelonephritis and renal scarring.

references.citation: Belko NA, Pohl HG. Pediatric Urinary Tract Infections. Urol Clin North Am. 2024;51(4):537-549. PMID 39349021. doi:10.1016/j.ucl.2024.06.004.
references.note: Review: neurogenic bladder conveys an increased risk of urinary tract infection; in the obstructed/refluxing bladder, UTI and stasis are the standard drivers of upper-tract dilatation and pyelonephritis.

PMID 34402323. doi:10.1177/21925682211037270.
references.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-13 evidence for the bounded degenerative-disc-disease to radiculopathy proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.

references.citation: Ruschel LG, Agnoletto GJ, Aragao A, Duarte JS, de Oliveira MF, Teles AR. Lumbar disc herniation with contralateral radiculopathy: a systematic review on pathophysiology and surgical strategies. Neurosurg Rev. 2021 Apr;44(2):1071-1081. doi:10.1007/s10143-020-01294-3. PMID 32281018.
references.note: Added pathophysiology anchor, registered as the MECHANISM source because it sets out how a herniated disc produces radicular pain and deficit through mechanical compression of the nerve root and dorsal root ganglion compounded by local inflammatory mediators, and because it documents contralateral presentations that simple one-sided compression cannot explain. references.citation: Knoers N, Lemmink H. Hereditary Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus. GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; 2000 Feb 12 [updated 2020 Feb 27]. PMID 20301356.
references.note: GeneReviews: inability to concentrate urine produces polyuria; short stature and secondary dilatation of the ureters and bladder from the high urine volume are common in untreated individuals; annual kidney ultrasound surveillance for hydronephrosis and megacystis is recommended; reducing urine production and scheduled voiding may prevent or reduce serious renal, ureteral, or bladder dilatation.

references.citation: Wang X, Ying X, Zhang F, Li X, Chen G, Zhou Z, Liao L. Upper urinary dilatation and treatment of 26 patients with diabetes insipidus: A single-center retrospective study. Front Endocrinol (Lausanne). 2022;13:941453. PMID 35937824.
references.note: Retrospective cohort (n=26 DI patients with upper urinary tract dilatation): video-urodynamics showed mean bladder capacity 575 mL with compliance 51.5 cmH2O and post-void residual >100 mL in 42.3%; neurogenic bladder was present in 23.1%; bladder distension, trabeculation, and decreased/absent sensations were common features; treatment improved dilatation grades and renal function.

references.citation: Duicu C, Pitea AM, Sasaran OM, Cozea I, Man L, Banescu C. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus in children (Review). Exp Ther Med. 2021;22(1):746. PMID 34055061.
references.note: Pediatric NDI review: without treatment most patients present with urological complications including megacystis, trabeculated bladder, hydroureter, and hydronephrosis; treatment combines sufficient water intake, low-sodium diet, and thiazide diuretics to reduce urine output.

references.citation: Azouvi P, Arnould A, Dromer E, Vallat-Azouvi C. Neuropsychology of traumatic brain injury: An expert overview. Rev Neurol (Paris). 2017;173(7-8):461-472. PMID 28847474.
references.note: Expert overview: patients who survive moderate-to-severe TBI frequently suffer a wide range of cognitive deficits and behavioral changes due to diffuse axonal injury - slowed information processing, impaired long-term memory, attention, working memory, executive function, social cognition, and self-awareness; mental fatigue frequently exacerbates the deficits.

references.citation: Su E, Bell M. Diffuse Axonal Injury. In: Translational Research in Traumatic Brain Injury. CRC Press/Taylor and Francis; 2016. PMID 26583181.
references.note: DAI review chapter: widespread axonal damage produces deficits in cerebral connectivity that may or may not recover; DAI is a component of injury in 40%-50% of TBI hospital admissions, commonly affecting brainstem, parasagittal white matter, and corpus callosum, and is increasingly recognized as an important cause of long-term disability.

references.citation: Pavlovic D, Pekic S, Stojanovic M, Popovic V. Traumatic brain injury: neuropathological, neurocognitive and neurobehavioral sequelae. Pituitary. 2019;22(3):270-282. PMID 30929221.
references.note: Sequelae review: DAI is visible only with advanced neuroimaging (DTI for white-matter pathology, SWI for microbleeds); chronic TBI patients have lower neuropsychological scores and higher mental-distress symptoms; TBI-related hypopituitarism overlaps with and can mimic cognitive disability - recorded as a competing cause requiring endocrine evaluation.

references.citation: Ammirati E, Palazzini M, Lehtonen J, et al. Natural History of Patients With Histologically Proven Acute Eosinophilic Myocarditis. Circulation. 2026 Mar 3;153(9):634-652. PMID 41645905.
references.note: International 53-center retrospective cohort of 156 biopsy-proven acute eosinophilic myocarditis patients: median LVEF 32% at presentation, high in-hospital and midterm mortality or heart transplantation, peripheral eosinophilia absent in 42.6% - the natural-history quantification anchor.

references.citation: Ammirati E, Selimi A, Palazzini M, et al. Acute and Chronic Myocarditis in Men and Women. Curr Heart Fail Rep. 2026 Jun 24;23(1):28. PMID 42340531.
references.note: Review: eosinophilic myocarditis in men predominate (67-82%) with distinct etiologic spectra across acute myocarditis subtypes - the etiologic-heterogeneity and demographic anchor.

references.citation: Aljudaibi A, Dutta K, Allam S, et al. Case Report: When inotropy backfires - dobutamine-associated eosinophilic myocarditis. Front Cardiovasc Med. 2026;13:1781601. PMID 42147059.
references.note: Case report of hypersensitivity eosinophilic myocarditis presenting as refractory cardiogenic shock requiring LVAD, resolving after drug withdrawal and corticosteroids - the drug-hypersensitivity mechanism and reversibility guard anchor, used with the case-report-class guard.

references.citation: Pregun I, Hritz I, Tulassay Z, Herszenyi L. Peptic esophageal stricture: medical treatment. Dig Dis. 2009;27(1):31-37. PMID 19439958.
references.note: Review of peptic stricture management: dilation and surgery are the therapeutic mainstays for the mechanical narrowing, and healing coexistent esophagitis with PPI reduces repeated dilations - the stricture-as-obstruction anchor.

references.citation: Cohen DL, Bermont A, Richter V, Shirin H. Real world management of esophageal ulcers: analysis of their presentation, complications and outcomes. Acta Gastroenterol Belg. 2021 Jul-Sep;84(3):417-422. PMID 34599565.
references.note: 11-year 100-patient esophageal-ulcer series: most ulcers due to gastroesophageal reflux with stricture the principal chronic sequela - the ulcer-to-stricture-to-dysphagia outcome anchor.

references.citation: Pearson EG, Downey EC, Barnhart DC, et al. Reflux esophageal stricture - a review of 30 years' experience in children. J Pediatr Surg. 2010 Dec;45(12):2356-2360. PMID 21129544.
references.note: 30-year 114-child series: reflux strictures requiring 486 dilations with refractory disease needing surgery - the severity-burden anchor for stricture dysphagia.

references.citation: Wald A. Management and prevention of fecal impaction. Curr Gastroenterol Rep. 2008 Oct;10(5):499-501. PMID 18799126.
references.note: Management review listing fecal incontinence among the clinical manifestations of fecal impaction alongside distention, obstruction, and stercoral complications - the impaction-manifestation anchor.

references.citation: Wald A. Fecal incontinence. Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol. 2005 Aug;8(4):319-324. PMID 16009033.
references.note: Fecal-incontinence review documenting fecal impaction with overflow incontinence as identifiable by history and examination and appropriately treatable - the disimpaction-response dependency anchor.

references.citation: Fox RA. Atypical presentation of geriatric infections. Geriatrics. 1988 May;43(5):58-64. PMID 3360329.
references.note: Geriatric presentation series documenting fecal impaction with incontinence as a recognized clinical presentation in elderly patients - the presentation-confirmation anchor.

references.citation: Naito Y, Yoshikawa T. Molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in Helicobacter pylori-induced inflammation and oxidative stress. Free Radic Biol Med. 2002;33(3):323-336. PMID 12126754.
references.note: Mechanisms review documenting that Helicobacter pylori infection leads to chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and gastric neoplasia with outcomes determined by the severity and distribution of inflammation - antral-type gastritis with excessive acid secretion and high duodenal-ulcer risk - the mechanism and distribution anchor.

references.citation: Ford AC, Gurusamy KS, Delaney B, et al. Eradication therapy for peptic ulcer disease in Helicobacter pylori-positive people. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2016;4(4):CD003840. PMID 27092708.
references.note: Cochrane review documenting that 95% of duodenal and 70% of gastric ulcers are associated with Helicobacter pylori and that eradication reduces ulcer relapse - the association-and-treatment-response anchor.

references.citation: Tomtitchong P, Siribumrungwong B, Vilaichone RK, et al. Systematic review and meta-analysis: Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy after simple closure of perforated duodenal ulcer. Helicobacter. 2012;17(2):148-152. PMID 22404446.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis documenting pooled one-year ulcer recurrence of 5.2% after eradication therapy following simple closure of perforated duodenal ulcer versus higher recurrence without eradication - the recurrence-prevention anchor.

references.citation: Kundnani NR, Kumar A, Sharma A, et al. Impact of Early Diagnosis and Immunosuppressive Therapy on Giant Cell Myocarditis Outcomes: A Review. Life (Basel). 2026;16(4):575. PMID 42073389.
references.note: Review documenting that giant cell myocarditis clinical onset is new-onset heart failure refractory to usual therapy with a frequently fulminant severe course, and that without rapid diagnosis and immunosuppressive therapy the disease runs a fulminant often fatal course - the presenting-syndrome and course anchor.

references.citation: Sacher AC, Ahmed R, Kung A, et al. Early Recognition of Giant Cell Myocarditis in a Patient With Fascicular Ventricular Tachycardia. JACC Case Rep. 2025;30(31):105333. PMID 41072973.
references.note: Biopsy-confirmed case report documenting giant cell myocarditis as a rare rapidly progressive inflammatory cardiomyopathy often manifesting with ventricular arrhythmias or heart failure with rapid clinical deterioration - the biopsy-confirmed phenotype anchor.

references.citation: Harling LC, Wacker M, Ruhparwar A, et al. Giant cell myocarditis in an 18-year-old patient with new-onset systemic lupus erythematosus: A fatal case of rapidly progressing heart failure. Lupus. 2026;35(10):1090-1098. PMID 42393943.
references.note: Case report documenting giant cell myocarditis presenting with biventricular heart failure that deteriorated rapidly to death before transplantation - the biventricular-failure case anchor.

references.citation: Kuiper J, de Herder WW, Feelders RA, et al. Approach to the patient with primary hyperglucagonemia. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2026. PMID 42766419.
references.note: Clinical approach review documenting that glucagonoma syndrome presents clinically by diabetes mellitus, weight loss, thromboembolic complications, and necrolytic migratory erythema, with diagnosis requiring elevated fasting plasma glucagon levels and tumor localization - the syndrome-definition and biochemical-criteria anchor.

references.citation: Perrier M, Brugel M, Gérard L, et al. Characteristics and treatment options of glucagonomas: a national study from the French Reference Center for Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors. Eur J Endocrinol. 2023;189(6):575-583. PMID 38039101.
references.note: National cohort study defining glucagonoma by major criteria including recent-onset diabetes, documenting diabetes at diagnosis in 50% and weight loss in 68.4% of patients, with partial or complete resolution of glucagonoma symptoms after treatment - the prevalence and treatment-response anchor.

references.citation: Anelli S, Mazzilli R, Zamponi V, et al. Glucagonoma and Glucagonoma Syndrome: An Updated Review. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2025;103(4):417-426. PMID 40613421.
references.note: Updated review of 74 glucagonoma patients documenting diabetes mellitus at presentation in 70.3% (50/74) with necrolytic migratory erythema in 93.2% and weight loss among the core features - the series-prevalence anchor.

references.citation: Otto CM, Nishimura RA, Bonow RO, et al. 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines. Circulation. 2021 Feb 2;143(5):e72-e227. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000923. PMID 33332150.
references.note: Guideline-level natural-history and management framework in which progressive valvular stenosis or regurgitation produces pressure or volume overload with compensatory chamber remodeling and symptomatic heart failure - the clinical-consensus anchor for a probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Vahanian A, Beyersdorf F, Praz F, et al. 2021 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease. Eur Heart J. 2022 Feb 12;43(7):561-632. PMID 34453165.
references.note: European guideline framework for the management of valvular heart disease, documenting the progression of valvular stenosis and regurgitation to symptomatic heart failure and its management - the independent-guideline corroboration anchor for the probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Demirbilek H, Hussain K. Congenital Hyperinsulinism: Diagnosis and Treatment Update. J Clin Res Pediatr Endocrinol. 2017 Dec 30;9(Suppl 2):69-87. doi:10.4274/jcrpe.2017.S007. PMID 29280746.
references.note: Congenital-hyperinsulinism diagnosis and treatment update defining hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia as inappropriate insulin secretion at low plasma glucose leading to severe and persistent hypoglycaemia, with suppressed ketogenesis from insulin's inhibitory effect - the mechanism anchor for the probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Giri D, Hawton K, Senniappan S. Congenital hyperinsulinism: recent updates on molecular mechanisms, diagnosis and management. J Pediatr Endocrinol Metab. 2021 Sep 21;35(3):279-296. doi:10.1515/jpem-2021-0369. PMID 34547194.
references.note: Congenital-hyperinsulinism update describing unregulated insulin release leading to hypoglycaemia as the most frequent cause of persistent and severe hypoglycaemia in the neonatal period and early childhood - the independent corroboration anchor.

references.citation: Arya VB, Mohammed Z, Blankenstein O, De Lonlay P, Hussain K. Hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia. Horm Metab Res. 2014 Mar;46(3):157-170. doi:10.1055/s-0034-1367063. PMID 24557504.
references.note: Review of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia stating that insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells becomes unregulated in the disorder so that it persists despite low blood glucose, and recording that in adults an insulinoma is the commonest cause of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia - the explicit insulinoma-as-cause statement anchoring the edge.

references.citation: Shah P, Rahman SA, Demirbilek H, Guemes M, Hussain K. Hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia in children and adults. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2017 Sep;5(9):729-742. doi:10.1016/S2213-8587(16)30323-0. PMID 27915035.
references.note: Lancet review stating that in hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia insulin secretion becomes dysregulated and uncoupled from glucose metabolism so that it persists at low plasma glucose, and that in adults the disorder accounts for 0.5-5.0% of hypoglycaemia cases and can be due either to beta-cell tumours (insulinomas) or beta-cell hyperplasia - the mechanism and adult-cause anchor.

references.citation: Pelsma ICMP et al. Quality of care evaluation in non-functioning pituitary adenoma with chiasm compression: visual outcomes and timing of intervention clinical recommendations based on a systematic literature review and cohort study. Pituitary. 2020;23(4):417-429. PMID 32419072
references.note: Systematic review of 44 studies involving 4,789 patients with nonfunctioning pituitary macroadenoma/chiasmal compression evaluated visual dysfunction and outcomes after decompression. Supports an anatomy-specific compressive visual pathway, not visual impairment from every pituitary neoplasm.

references.citation: Humbert M, Kovacs G, Hoeper MM, et al. 2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2022;43(38):3618-3731. PMID 36017548
references.note: Multisociety guideline classifies pulmonary hypertension by mechanism, notes that symptoms are linked to right-ventricular dysfunction, and includes dedicated management of advanced right-ventricular failure in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Supports a phenotype-bounded progression pathway, not generic all-PH-to-CHF causation.

references.note: Clinical series of 180 patients with urethral stenosis reporting renal-ureteral complications including ureterohydronephrosis; supports an obstruction-to-upper-tract-dilation pathway but not automatic individual causation.

references.note: Systematic review of 66 studies reported postoperative continence impairment in 12.7% of patients undergoing sphincter-cutting treatment for simple anal fistula; study quality was generally low. references.citation: Scheffel TB, Diz FM, Wieck A, Begnini KR, da Costa JC. The molecular landscape of glioblastoma-associated epilepsy. J Mol Med (Berl). 2025;103(8):923-933. PMID 40576825. doi:10.1007/s00109-025-02567-4.
references.note: Review of glioblastoma-associated epilepsy documenting seizures as a common symptom reflecting tumor microenvironment interactions, with molecular mechanisms including increased glutamate release, ion-channel dysfunction, inflammation, and shared synaptic and immune pathways; supports the direct tumor-driven seizure mechanism, not a statistical comorbidity framing.

references.citation: Kerkhof M, Benit C, Duran-Pena A, Vecht CJ. Seizures in oligodendroglial tumors. CNS Oncol. 2015;4(5):347-356. PMID 26478444. doi:10.2217/cns.15.29.
references.note: Review reporting epilepsy development in more than 70 to 90 percent of oligodendroglial tumors with glutamate and GABA metabolism alterations implicated in glioma-associated epilepsy and seizure outcomes after surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy; supports the tumor-driven seizure physiology within the glial-tumor spectrum, not individual claim determination.

references.citation: Moradi et al., BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders (2025), PMID 40380123
references.note: Systematic review of 20 studies focused on surgically treated lumbar disc herniation/CES populations; persistent sexual dysfunction was common after CES and erectile dysfunction was the most frequently reported male sexual disorder. Supports this bounded postoperative population, not unrestricted generalization across all CES etiologies or automatic individual causation.

references.citation: Xu T, Yu X, Ou S, Liu X, Yuan J, Huang H, Yang J, He L, Chen Y. Risk factors for posttraumatic epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Epilepsy Behav. 2017;67:1-6. PMID 28076834. doi:10.1016/j.yebeh.2016.10.026.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of PTE risk factors reporting brain contusion as a strong risk factor (RR 2.35, 95% CI 1.69-3.28) among TBI-related neuroimaging findings, with elevated risk sustained beyond ten years; supports the direct lesion-seizure pathway at the highest evidence tier available for this edge.

references.citation: Wang H, Xin T, Sun X, Wang S, Guo H, Holton-Burke C, Pang Q. Post-traumatic seizures—a prospective, multicenter, large case study after head injury in China. Epilepsy Res. 2013;107(3):272-278. PMID 24239245. doi:10.1016/j.eplepsyres.2013.10.006.
references.note: Prospective multicenter cohort (3,093 TBI patients, two-year follow-up) identifying frontal-temporal lobar contusion among three independent multivariate predictors of post-traumatic seizures, with a cumulative 24-month seizure rate of 9.8% establishing population incidence; independently corroborates the meta-analytic finding.

references.citation: Lutkenhoff ES, Shrestha V, Ruiz Tejeda J, Real C, McArthur DL, Duncan D, La Rocca M, Garner R, Toga AW, Vespa PM, Monti MM. Early brain biomarkers of post-traumatic seizures: initial report of the multicentre epilepsy bioinformatics study for antiepileptogenic therapy (EpiBioS4Rx) prospective study. J Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry. 2020;91(11):1154-1157. PMID 32848013. doi:10.1136/jnnp-2020-322780.
references.note: Multicenter prospective cohort (96 moderate-to-severe TBI patients) associating focal cortical volume deficits, including hippocampal and temporal-cortex thinning, with early and late post-traumatic seizures; supports the lesion-burden gradient underlying the pathway, at biomarker-association strength.

references.citation: Chinese Society of Hepatology et al., Consensus on the diagnosis and treatment of hepatic fibrosis (2019), J Dig Dis. 2020;21:127-138. PMID 32108989
references.note: Evidence-based consensus describing hepatic fibrosis as a key developmental step across chronic liver diseases leading to cirrhosis; supports a fibrosis-progression pathway, not an automatic individual nexus.

references.citation: Roman GC. Vascular dementia may be the most common form of dementia in the elderly. J Neurol Sci. 2002;203-204:7-10. PMID 12417349. doi:10.1016/s0022-510x(02)00252-6.

references.citation: Fallo et al., Diagnosis and management of hypertension in patients with Cushing's syndrome: a position statement and consensus of the Working Group on Endocrine Hypertension of the European Society of Hypertension, J Hypertens. 2022;40(11):2085-2101. PMID 35950979
references.note: Endocrine-hypertension consensus states that hypertension is common in Cushing's syndrome and may persist after normalization of hormone excess or steroid withdrawal; supports a disease-specific endocrine hypertension pathway with individual diagnosis and chronology safeguards.

references.citation: Leslie SW, Aeddula NR. Vesicoureteral Reflux. StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing; updated 2024 Apr 30. PMID 33085409.
references.note: StatPearls review: neurogenic bladder is a recognized cause of vesicoureteral reflux, and high-pressure bladder conditions are key predictors of additional renal damage and scarring; reflux nephropathy accounts for about 5% of pediatric renal transplants.

references.citation: Wu CQ, Franco I. Management of vesicoureteral reflux in neurogenic bladder. Investig Clin Urol. 2017;58(Suppl 1):S54-S58. PMID 28612061. doi:10.4111/icu.2017.58.S1.S54.
references.note: Review: VUR in neurogenic bladder develops through a defective ureterovesical junction or an overwhelmed normal UVJ mechanism caused by bladder dysfunction; VUR is a significant risk factor for pyelonephritis and renal scarring.

references.citation: Belko NA, Pohl HG. Pediatric Urinary Tract Infections. Urol Clin North Am. 2024;51(4):537-549. PMID 39349021. doi:10.1016/j.ucl.2024.06.004.
references.note: Review: neurogenic bladder conveys an increased risk of urinary tract infection; in the obstructed/refluxing bladder, UTI and stasis are the standard drivers of upper-tract dilatation and pyelonephritis.

references.citation: Ocampo-Navia MI, Perez-Mendez W, Rodriguez-Alvarez MP, Chadid-Contreras J, Vergara MF. Dandy-Walker syndrome: an updated literature review. Childs Nerv Syst. 2025;41(1):194. PMID 40445443. doi:10.1007/s00381-025-06842-0.
references.note: Updated review: DWS occurs in 1 in 25,000-35,000 live births and often presents with hydrocephalus and other CNS anomalies; management involves treating hydrocephalus, and prognosis hinges on associated malformations.

references.citation: Spennato P, Mirone G, Nastro A, Buonocore MC, Ruggiero C, Trischitta V, Aliberti F, Cinalli G. Hydrocephalus in Dandy-Walker malformation. Childs Nerv Syst. 2011;27(10):1665-1681. PMID 21928031. doi:10.1007/s00381-011-1544-4.
references.note: Definitive review dedicated to the hydrocephalus-DWM relationship: therapeutic control of hydrocephalus (single shunting of ventricle or cyst, or endoscopic third ventriculostomy) is effective, and prognosis and intellectual outcome depend on associated malformations and the adequate control of hydrocephalus.

references.citation: Bokhari I, Rehman L, Hassan S, Hashim MS. Dandy-Walker Malformation: A Clinical and Surgical Outcome Analysis. J Coll Physicians Surg Pak. 2015;25(6):431-433. PMID 26100996.
references.note: Surgical case series (n=70): hydrocephalus was present in all patients as the predominant presenting feature; shunt malfunction and infection were the commonest post-treatment complications.

references.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-13 evidence for the bounded degenerative-disc-disease to radiculopathy proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.

references.note: Added pathophysiology anchor, registered as the MECHANISM source because it sets out how a herniated disc produces radicular pain and deficit through mechanical compression of the nerve root and dorsal root ganglion compounded by local inflammatory mediators, and because it documents contralateral presentations that simple one-sided compression cannot explain. references.citation: Erectile and Ejaculatory Dysfunction Associated with Use of Psychotropic Drugs: A Systematic Review, PMID 34247952
references.note: Systematic review of randomized trials found antidepressant therapy associated with erectile dysfunction overall (OR 2.28, 95% CI 1.31-3.97), while effects differed by drug class; supports agent-specific medication research, not an automatic individual nexus.

references.citation: Knoers N, Lemmink H. Hereditary Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus. GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; 2000 Feb 12 [updated 2020 Feb 27]. PMID 20301356.
references.note: GeneReviews: inability to concentrate urine produces polyuria; short stature and secondary dilatation of the ureters and bladder from the high urine volume are common in untreated individuals; annual kidney ultrasound surveillance for hydronephrosis and megacystis is recommended; reducing urine production and scheduled voiding may prevent or reduce serious renal, ureteral, or bladder dilatation.

references.citation: Wang X, Ying X, Zhang F, Li X, Chen G, Zhou Z, Liao L. Upper urinary dilatation and treatment of 26 patients with diabetes insipidus: A single-center retrospective study. Front Endocrinol (Lausanne). 2022;13:941453. PMID 35937824.
references.note: Retrospective cohort (n=26 DI patients with upper urinary tract dilatation): video-urodynamics showed mean bladder capacity 575 mL with compliance 51.5 cmH2O and post-void residual >100 mL in 42.3%; neurogenic bladder was present in 23.1%; bladder distension, trabeculation, and decreased/absent sensations were common features; treatment improved dilatation grades and renal function.

references.citation: Duicu C, Pitea AM, Sasaran OM, Cozea I, Man L, Banescu C. Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus in children (Review). Exp Ther Med. 2021;22(1):746. PMID 34055061.
references.note: Pediatric NDI review: without treatment most patients present with urological complications including megacystis, trabeculated bladder, hydroureter, and hydronephrosis; treatment combines sufficient water intake, low-sodium diet, and thiazide diuretics to reduce urine output.

references.citation: Azouvi P, Arnould A, Dromer E, Vallat-Azouvi C. Neuropsychology of traumatic brain injury: An expert overview. Rev Neurol (Paris). 2017;173(7-8):461-472. PMID 28847474.
references.note: Expert overview: patients who survive moderate-to-severe TBI frequently suffer a wide range of cognitive deficits and behavioral changes due to diffuse axonal injury - slowed information processing, impaired long-term memory, attention, working memory, executive function, social cognition, and self-awareness; mental fatigue frequently exacerbates the deficits.

references.citation: Su E, Bell M. Diffuse Axonal Injury. In: Translational Research in Traumatic Brain Injury. CRC Press/Taylor and Francis; 2016. PMID 26583181.
references.note: DAI review chapter: widespread axonal damage produces deficits in cerebral connectivity that may or may not recover; DAI is a component of injury in 40%-50% of TBI hospital admissions, commonly affecting brainstem, parasagittal white matter, and corpus callosum, and is increasingly recognized as an important cause of long-term disability.

references.citation: Pavlovic D, Pekic S, Stojanovic M, Popovic V. Traumatic brain injury: neuropathological, neurocognitive and neurobehavioral sequelae. Pituitary. 2019;22(3):270-282. PMID 30929221.
references.note: Sequelae review: DAI is visible only with advanced neuroimaging (DTI for white-matter pathology, SWI for microbleeds); chronic TBI patients have lower neuropsychological scores and higher mental-distress symptoms; TBI-related hypopituitarism overlaps with and can mimic cognitive disability - recorded as a competing cause requiring endocrine evaluation.

references.citation: Wang Y, Ma Y, Wang Y, et al. Age-stratified clinical characteristics and long-term neurological outcomes of pediatric herpes simplex virus encephalitis: a longitudinal cohort study. Front Neurol. 2026;17:1882046. PMID 42564238.
references.note: Longitudinal cohort of 56 confirmed pediatric HSE patients (median follow-up 62.5 months): post-encephalitic epilepsy in 53.6% with 63.3% drug-refractory, plus acquired anti-NMDAR encephalitis in 17.9% - the lesion-to-epilepsy quantification anchor for a necrotizing, limbic-tropic etiology.

references.citation: Fillatre P, Mailles A, Stahl JP, et al. Functional outcome after infectious encephalitis: a longitudinal multicentre cohort study. Clin Microbiol Infect. 2025 Mar;31(3):459-465. PMID 39522606.
references.note: ENCEIF prospective multicenter cohort (322 survivors, 896 modified-Rankin evaluations): substantial residual neurological disability after infectious encephalitis - the outcome-burden anchor supporting the direct-injury proposition for the infectious subgroup.

references.citation: Hawkes MA, Carabenciov ID, Wijdicks EFM, Rabinstein AA. Outcomes in Patients With Severe West Nile Neuroinvasive Disease. Crit Care Med. 2018 Sep;46(9):e955-e958. PMID 29985213.
references.note: Long-term follow-up of severe West Nile neuroinvasive disease: persistent functional disability and cognitive impairment in many survivors - the etiologic-heterogeneity guard anchor (severe necrotizing presentations carry the injury pathway; mild systemic presentations do not).

references.citation: Ammirati E, Palazzini M, Lehtonen J, et al. Natural History of Patients With Histologically Proven Acute Eosinophilic Myocarditis. Circulation. 2026 Mar 3;153(9):634-652. PMID 41645905.
references.note: International 53-center retrospective cohort of 156 biopsy-proven acute eosinophilic myocarditis patients: median LVEF 32% at presentation, high in-hospital and midterm mortality or heart transplantation, peripheral eosinophilia absent in 42.6% - the natural-history quantification anchor.

references.citation: Ammirati E, Selimi A, Palazzini M, et al. Acute and Chronic Myocarditis in Men and Women. Curr Heart Fail Rep. 2026 Jun 24;23(1):28. PMID 42340531.
references.note: Review: eosinophilic myocarditis in men predominate (67-82%) with distinct etiologic spectra across acute myocarditis subtypes - the etiologic-heterogeneity and demographic anchor.

references.citation: Aljudaibi A, Dutta K, Allam S, et al. Case Report: When inotropy backfires - dobutamine-associated eosinophilic myocarditis. Front Cardiovasc Med. 2026;13:1781601. PMID 42147059.
references.note: Case report of hypersensitivity eosinophilic myocarditis presenting as refractory cardiogenic shock requiring LVAD, resolving after drug withdrawal and corticosteroids - the drug-hypersensitivity mechanism and reversibility guard anchor, used with the case-report-class guard.

references.citation: Pregun I, Hritz I, Tulassay Z, Herszenyi L. Peptic esophageal stricture: medical treatment. Dig Dis. 2009;27(1):31-37. PMID 19439958.
references.note: Review of peptic stricture management: dilation and surgery are the therapeutic mainstays for the mechanical narrowing, and healing coexistent esophagitis with PPI reduces repeated dilations - the stricture-as-obstruction anchor.

references.citation: Cohen DL, Bermont A, Richter V, Shirin H. Real world management of esophageal ulcers: analysis of their presentation, complications and outcomes. Acta Gastroenterol Belg. 2021 Jul-Sep;84(3):417-422. PMID 34599565.
references.note: 11-year 100-patient esophageal-ulcer series: most ulcers due to gastroesophageal reflux with stricture the principal chronic sequela - the ulcer-to-stricture-to-dysphagia outcome anchor.

references.note: 30-year 114-child series: reflux strictures requiring 486 dilations with refractory disease needing surgery - the severity-burden anchor for stricture dysphagia.

references.citation: Pregun I, Hritz I, Tulassay Z, Herszenyi L. Peptic esophageal stricture: medical treatment. Dig Dis. 2009;27(1):31-37. PMID 19439958.
references.note: Review: healing the coexistent esophagitis is essential to peptic-stricture outcome and effective acid suppression reduces the need for repeated dilations - the inflammation-dependency anchor.

references.citation: Cohen DL, Bermont A, Richter V, Shirin H. Real world management of esophageal ulcers: analysis of their presentation, complications and outcomes. Acta Gastroenterol Belg. 2021 Jul-Sep;84(3):417-422. PMID 34599565.
references.note: 11-year 100-patient series: most esophageal ulcers are reflux-related with stricture the principal chronic sequela - the ulcer-to-stricture outcome anchor.

references.citation: Pearson EG, Downey EC, Barnhart DC, et al. Reflux esophageal stricture - a review of 30 years' experience in children. J Pediatr Surg. 2010 Dec;45(12):2356-2360. PMID 21129544.
references.note: 30-year 114-child series of reflux esophagitis strictures requiring 486 dilations with refractory disease needing surgery - the untreated-inflammation progression anchor.

references.citation: Wald A. Management and prevention of fecal impaction. Curr Gastroenterol Rep. 2008 Oct;10(5):499-501. PMID 18799126.
references.note: Management review listing fecal incontinence among the clinical manifestations of fecal impaction alongside distention, obstruction, and stercoral complications - the impaction-manifestation anchor.

references.citation: Wald A. Fecal incontinence. Curr Treat Options Gastroenterol. 2005 Aug;8(4):319-324. PMID 16009033.

references.note: Geriatric presentation series documenting fecal impaction with incontinence as a recognized clinical presentation in elderly patients - the presentation-confirmation anchor.

references.citation: Norton JA. Surgical treatment and prognosis of gastrinoma. Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol. 2005;19(5):799-805. PMID 16253901.
references.note: Review defining Zollinger-Ellison syndrome as severe peptic ulcer disease and diarrhea caused by gastric acid hypersecretion secondary to the gastrin-secreting neuroendocrine tumor, with tumor-size-based malignant potential and surgical cure settings - the causal-definition anchor.

references.citation: Wilcox CM, Seay T, Arcury JT, et al. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: presentation, response to therapy, and outcome. Dig Liver Dis. 2011;43(6):439-443. PMID 21193359.
references.note: Twenty-year prospective lansoprazole trial of 72 patients documenting stereotypical presentation with ulcer disease, median nine-year symptom delay before diagnosis, gastric acid analysis follow-up, and sustained antisecretory response - the prospective presentation-and-response anchor.

references.citation: Guarnotta V, Martini C, Davì MV, et al. The Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: is there a role for somatostatin analogues in the treatment of the gastrinoma? Endocrine. 2018;60(1):15-27. PMID 29019150.
references.note: Review documenting that treatment of gastrinoma and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is aimed at controlling acid hypersecretion and tumor progression, with proton pump inhibition as the cornerstone of syndrome control - the acid-control and prevention anchor.

references.citation: Naito Y, Yoshikawa T. Molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in Helicobacter pylori-induced inflammation and oxidative stress. Free Radic Biol Med. 2002;33(3):323-336. PMID 12126754.
references.note: Mechanisms review documenting that Helicobacter pylori infection leads to chronic gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, and gastric neoplasia with outcomes determined by the severity and distribution of inflammation - antral-type gastritis with excessive acid secretion and high duodenal-ulcer risk - the mechanism and distribution anchor.

references.citation: Ford AC, Gurusamy KS, Delaney B, et al. Eradication therapy for peptic ulcer disease in Helicobacter pylori-positive people. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2016;4(4):CD003840. PMID 27092708.
references.note: Cochrane review documenting that 95% of duodenal and 70% of gastric ulcers are associated with Helicobacter pylori and that eradication reduces ulcer relapse - the association-and-treatment-response anchor.

references.citation: Tomtitchong P, Siribumrungwong B, Vilaichone RK, et al. Systematic review and meta-analysis: Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy after simple closure of perforated duodenal ulcer. Helicobacter. 2012;17(2):148-152. PMID 22404446.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis documenting pooled one-year ulcer recurrence of 5.2% after eradication therapy following simple closure of perforated duodenal ulcer versus higher recurrence without eradication - the recurrence-prevention anchor.

references.citation: Kundnani NR, Kumar A, Sharma A, et al. Impact of Early Diagnosis and Immunosuppressive Therapy on Giant Cell Myocarditis Outcomes: A Review. Life (Basel). 2026;16(4):575. PMID 42073389.
references.note: Review documenting that giant cell myocarditis clinical onset is new-onset heart failure refractory to usual therapy with a frequently fulminant severe course, and that without rapid diagnosis and immunosuppressive therapy the disease runs a fulminant often fatal course - the presenting-syndrome and course anchor.

references.citation: Sacher AC, Ahmed R, Kung A, et al. Early Recognition of Giant Cell Myocarditis in a Patient With Fascicular Ventricular Tachycardia. JACC Case Rep. 2025;30(31):105333. PMID 41072973.
references.note: Biopsy-confirmed case report documenting giant cell myocarditis as a rare rapidly progressive inflammatory cardiomyopathy often manifesting with ventricular arrhythmias or heart failure with rapid clinical deterioration - the biopsy-confirmed phenotype anchor.

references.citation: Harling LC, Wacker M, Ruhparwar A, et al. Giant cell myocarditis in an 18-year-old patient with new-onset systemic lupus erythematosus: A fatal case of rapidly progressing heart failure. Lupus. 2026;35(10):1090-1098. PMID 42393943.
references.note: Case report documenting giant cell myocarditis presenting with biventricular heart failure that deteriorated rapidly to death before transplantation - the biventricular-failure case anchor.

references.citation: Kuiper J, de Herder WW, Feelders RA, et al. Approach to the patient with primary hyperglucagonemia. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2026. PMID 42766419.
references.note: Clinical approach review documenting that glucagonoma syndrome presents clinically by diabetes mellitus, weight loss, thromboembolic complications, and necrolytic migratory erythema, with diagnosis requiring elevated fasting plasma glucagon levels and tumor localization - the syndrome-definition and biochemical-criteria anchor.

references.citation: Perrier M, Brugel M, Gérard L, et al. Characteristics and treatment options of glucagonomas: a national study from the French Reference Center for Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors. Eur J Endocrinol. 2023;189(6):575-583. PMID 38039101.
references.note: National cohort study defining glucagonoma by major criteria including recent-onset diabetes, documenting diabetes at diagnosis in 50% and weight loss in 68.4% of patients, with partial or complete resolution of glucagonoma symptoms after treatment - the prevalence and treatment-response anchor.

references.citation: Anelli S, Mazzilli R, Zamponi V, et al. Glucagonoma and Glucagonoma Syndrome: An Updated Review. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2025;103(4):417-426. PMID 40613421.
references.note: Updated review of 74 glucagonoma patients documenting diabetes mellitus at presentation in 70.3% (50/74) with necrolytic migratory erythema in 93.2% and weight loss among the core features - the series-prevalence anchor.

references.citation: Catarina Oliveira A, Figueiredo R, Correia R, et al. Anti-glomerular basement membrane disease: A contemporary case series from a large university hospital. Nefrologia (Engl Ed). 2026;46(7):501522. PMID 42618193.
references.note: Contemporary case series documenting 92.6% renal replacement requirement at presentation, crescentic glomerulonephritis in 80% of biopsies, and limited renal recovery (18.5% of those presenting on renal replacement) with crescent burden above 40% and absent preserved glomeruli predicting poor outcome despite therapy - the renal-destruction and non-recovery anchor.

references.citation: Suhlrie A, van der Meijden WAG, Faguer S, et al. Outcomes in Children and Adults With Antiglomerular Basement Membrane Disease. Kidney Int Rep. 2026;11(5):106353. PMID 42006224.
references.note: Cohort of 72 children and adults with anti-GBM disease documenting rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with dialysis at diagnosis a strong predictor of outcome regardless of age under plasma-exchange-based treatment - the dialysis-outcome predictor anchor.

references.citation: Wang Y, Zhai Z, Wang L, et al. Rituximab is associated with accelerated dialysis independence in anti-glomerular basement membrane disease: a multicenter retrospective study. Front Immunol. 2026;17:1835889. PMID 42199438.
references.note: Multicenter study of 66 confirmed anti-GBM patients documenting dialysis independence in about half recovering, accelerated dialysis independence with rituximab addition, and a trend toward higher renal survival with initial dialysis dependency a predictor - the subset-recovery and treatment-response anchor that grounds the PROBABLE (not WELL_ESTABLISHED) ceiling.

references.citation: Shen J, Gill J, Shangguan M, Sampaio MS, Bunnapradist S. Outcomes of renal transplantation in recipients with Wegener's granulomatosis. Clin Transplant. 2011 May-Jun;25(3):380-7. PMID 20394635.
references.note: OPTN/UNOS analysis of 919 transplant recipients with end-stage renal disease caused by Wegener granulomatosis documenting it as the leading cause of rapidly-progressive-glomerulonephritis-induced end-stage renal disease - the registry-level renal-destruction attribution anchor.

references.citation: James KE, Xiao R, Merkel PA, Weiss PF. Clinical course and outcomes of childhood-onset granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Clin Exp Rheumatol. 2017 Mar-Apr;35 Suppl 103(1):202-208. PMID 27749233.
references.note: Retrospective cohort of 28 children with GPA documenting 37% at chronic kidney disease stage greater than 2 at median 3.3-year follow-up, renal failure accounting for most readmissions, and dialysis required at presentation in 14% despite 85% remission achievement with 11 subsequent flares - the progression, flare, and remission-stratification anchor.

references.citation: Sattui SE, Jiang B, Fu X, et al. The effects of age and frailty on the risks of end-stage renal disease, death, and severe infection in older adults with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis: a retrospective cohort study. Lancet Rheumatol. 2024 Nov;6(11):e771-e779. PMID 39305914.
references.note: Retrospective cohort of 234 older adults with incident ANCA-associated vasculitis documenting end-stage renal disease or death concentrated within two years of diagnosis with incidence rates stratified by age and frailty - the contemporary adult renal-outcome and chronology anchor.

references.citation: Tong J, Xu B, Zhang C, Dong Z. Surgical outcome for type I Guyon's canal syndrome with claw hand deformity: a review of 11 patients. Acta Neurochir (Wien). 2026 May 1;168(1):118. PMID 42065727.
references.note: Retrospective series of 11 type-I Guyon's canal syndrome patients with established claw hand deformity and intrinsic muscle weakness, documenting strength improvement in all hands, 72.7% regaining MRC grade 5 and complete deformity correction in 90.9% after decompression at minimum one-year follow-up - the atrophy-distribution and dechallenge-reversal anchor.

references.citation: Wang B, Zhao Y, Lu A, Chen C. Ulnar nerve deep branch compression by a ganglion: a review of nine cases. Injury. 2014 Jul;45(7):1126-30. PMID 24774037.
references.note: Review of nine cases documenting different degrees of muscular atrophy and weakness of the interossei and adductor pollicis without sensory loss, with mean symptom duration of 16 months (range 5-32) before surgery and grip and tip-pinch strength recovery after ganglion excision and decompression - the dose-duration atrophy and recovery anchor.

references.citation: Chen SH, Tsai TM. Ulnar tunnel syndrome. J Hand Surg Am. 2014 Mar;39(3):571-9. PMID 24559635.
references.note: Journal of Hand Surgery review of ulnar tunnel (Guyon's canal) syndrome documenting the compressive-neuropathy construct and the diagnostic difficulty from coexisting carpal tunnel syndrome, cubital tunnel syndrome, thoracic outlet syndrome, C8-T1 radiculopathy, and peripheral neuropathy - the mechanism and mimic-exclusion anchor.

references.citation: Otto CM, Nishimura RA, Bonow RO, et al. 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines. Circulation. 2021 Feb 2;143(5):e72-e227. doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000000923. PMID 33332150.
references.note: Guideline-level natural-history and management framework in which progressive valvular stenosis or regurgitation produces pressure or volume overload with compensatory chamber remodeling and symptomatic heart failure - the clinical-consensus anchor for a probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Vahanian A, Beyersdorf F, Praz F, et al. 2021 ESC/EACTS Guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease. Eur Heart J. 2022 Feb 12;43(7):561-632. PMID 34453165.
references.note: European guideline framework for the management of valvular heart disease, documenting the progression of valvular stenosis and regurgitation to symptomatic heart failure and its management - the independent-guideline corroboration anchor for the probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Barritt AS 4th, Qasim A, Kim Y, Miller SD, O'Donnell J, Johnston K. Prognostic value of liver histology in steatotic liver disease: a systematic literature review and meta-analysis. J Comp Eff Res. 2026 Sep 3:e260148. doi:10.57264/cer-2026-0148. PMID 42690133.
references.note: Systematic literature review and meta-analysis pooling 32 studies of histologic liver fibrosis in steatotic liver disease showing that higher fibrosis stage is associated with increasing risk of major adverse liver outcomes including cirrhosis, hepatic decompensation, and hepatocellular carcinoma - the meta-analytic natural-history anchor for a probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Wang X, Dong X, Qian L, Yang Z, Yang D, Niu Y. Non-invasive Tests for the Prediction of Liver-related Events in Patients with MASLD: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Radiol. 2026 Jul 22:S1076-6332(26)00476-9. doi:10.1016/j.acra.2026.06.068. PMID 42481370.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of non-invasive tests for the prediction of liver-related events in MASLD, documenting the progression of metabolic steatotic liver disease to cirrhosis and its complications - the independent corroboration anchor for the fibrosing-progression pathway.

references.citation: Demirbilek H, Hussain K. Congenital Hyperinsulinism: Diagnosis and Treatment Update. J Clin Res Pediatr Endocrinol. 2017 Dec 30;9(Suppl 2):69-87. doi:10.4274/jcrpe.2017.S007. PMID 29280746.
references.note: Congenital-hyperinsulinism diagnosis and treatment update defining hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia as inappropriate insulin secretion at low plasma glucose leading to severe and persistent hypoglycaemia, with suppressed ketogenesis from insulin's inhibitory effect - the mechanism anchor for the probable direct nexus.

references.citation: Giri D, Hawton K, Senniappan S. Congenital hyperinsulinism: recent updates on molecular mechanisms, diagnosis and management. J Pediatr Endocrinol Metab. 2021 Sep 21;35(3):279-296. doi:10.1515/jpem-2021-0369. PMID 34547194.
references.note: Congenital-hyperinsulinism update describing unregulated insulin release leading to hypoglycaemia as the most frequent cause of persistent and severe hypoglycaemia in the neonatal period and early childhood - the independent corroboration anchor.

references.citation: Bilezikian JP, Khan AA, Silverberg SJ, et al. Evaluation and Management of Primary Hyperparathyroidism: Summary Statement and Guidelines from the Fifth International Workshop. J Bone Miner Res. 2022;37(11):2293-2314. PMID 36245251
references.note: International guideline for primary hyperparathyroidism; supports renal evaluation for stone disease and uses nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis as clinically important renal involvement. The repository limits this pathway to confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism rather than generalizing it to secondary or tertiary hyperparathyroidism.

references.citation: Jones et al., 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults, Circulation. 2025;152(11):e114-e218. PMID 40811497
references.note: Current multidisciplinary guideline identifies high blood pressure as a modifiable risk factor for development of chronic kidney disease and provides CKD-specific hypertension management recommendations; supports a target-organ-damage research pathway while requiring individual renal etiology and chronology review.

references.citation: Jones et al., 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults, Circulation. 2025;152(11):e114-e218. PMID 40811497
references.note: Current guideline's heart-failure-prevention section describes antecedent hypertension, a dose-dependent BP-heart-failure association, and reduced heart-failure risk with long-term blood-pressure treatment; supports a hypertension-to-heart-failure progression pathway with individual etiology safeguards.

references.citation: Díez and Butler, Growing Heart Failure Burden of Hypertensive Heart Disease: A Call to Action, Hypertension. 2023;80:13-21. PMID 36082670
references.note: Condition-specific review describing hypertensive heart disease as a major cause of heart failure and addressing the HHD-to-HF clinical burden; supports disease-progression plausibility, not an automatic individual nexus.

references.citation: Rochira V, Antonio L, Vanderschueren D. EAA clinical guideline on management of bone health in the andrological outpatient clinic. Andrology. 2018;6(2):272-285. PMID 29499097
references.note: European Academy of Andrology practice guideline recognizes testosterone-deficiency-associated bone loss/frailty, recommends complete bone-health assessment and DXA in men with confirmed clinical hypogonadism, and notes that fracture-prevention efficacy of testosterone replacement is not established.

references.citation: Stevens DL, Bryant AE. Streptococcus pyogenes Impetigo, Erysipelas, and Cellulitis. In: Ferretti JJ, Stevens DL, Fischetti VA, editors. Streptococcus pyogenes: Basic Biology to Clinical Manifestations [Internet]. 2nd edition. Oklahoma City (OK): University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center; 2022 Oct 8. Chapter 23. PMID 36479753.
references.note: Reference chapter on group A streptococcal skin and soft-tissue infection stating that impetigo is a non-life-threatening infection but can result in post-streptococcal acute glomerulonephritis - the disease-specific complication statement anchoring the impetigo-to-nephritis proposition.

references.citation: Ilyas M, Tolaymat A. Changing epidemiology of acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis in Northeast Florida: a comparative study. Pediatr Nephrol. 2008 Jul;23(7):1101-1106. doi:10.1007/s00467-008-0778-1. PMID 18373105.
references.note: Comparative epidemiological study of paediatric acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis in which 66% of the earlier cohort had antecedent pyoderma (versus a recent cohort predominantly pharyngitis-associated) - the cohort-level antecedent-skin-infection anchor and the basis for the recorded era and population caveat.

references.citation: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Prognosis of Tricuspid Regurgitation After Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. PMID 34389210
references.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis found tricuspid-regurgitation deterioration after cardiac implantable electronic-device implantation and identified lead interference as a strong risk factor. Supports a transvenous lead-associated pathway, not automatic individual causation or application to leadless/epicardial systems.

references.citation: Arya VB, Mohammed Z, Blankenstein O, De Lonlay P, Hussain K. Hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia. Horm Metab Res. 2014 Mar;46(3):157-170. doi:10.1055/s-0034-1367063. PMID 24557504.
references.note: Review of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia stating that insulin secretion from pancreatic beta cells becomes unregulated in the disorder so that it persists despite low blood glucose, and recording that in adults an insulinoma is the commonest cause of hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia - the explicit insulinoma-as-cause statement anchoring the edge.

references.citation: Shah P, Rahman SA, Demirbilek H, Guemes M, Hussain K. Hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia in children and adults. Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2017 Sep;5(9):729-742. doi:10.1016/S2213-8587(16)30323-0. PMID 27915035.
references.note: Lancet review stating that in hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia insulin secretion becomes dysregulated and uncoupled from glucose metabolism so that it persists at low plasma glucose, and that in adults the disorder accounts for 0.5-5.0% of hypoglycaemia cases and can be due either to beta-cell tumours (insulinomas) or beta-cell hyperplasia - the mechanism and adult-cause anchor.

references.citation: Zhong J, Lan Y, Sun L, Zhao Z, Liu X, Shi J, Ren L, Zuo Q, Wei X, Dou X. Global prevalence of post-traumatic epilepsy in traumatic brain injury patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis (1997-2024). Neuroscience. 2025 Oct 1;584:180-189. doi:10.1016/j.neuroscience.2025.07.008. PMID 40835018.
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies and 505,720 patients reporting a pooled post-traumatic epilepsy prevalence of 9% (95% CI 8-11%), 15% under International League Against Epilepsy diagnostic criteria, 16% for severe cases, and 14% for early post-traumatic seizure studies, concluding that post-traumatic epilepsy is a common complication of traumatic brain injury - the quantitative prevalence anchor.

references.citation: Laing J, Gabbe B, Chen Z, Perucca P, Kwan P, O'Brien TJ. Risk Factors and Prognosis of Early Posttraumatic Seizures in Moderate to Severe Traumatic Brain Injury. JAMA Neurol. 2022 Apr 1;79(4):334-341. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2021.5420. PMID 35188950.
references.note: Registry-based cohort of 15,152 adults with moderate to severe traumatic brain injury with two-year follow-up in which 416 patients (2.7%) had early post-traumatic seizures, including 27 (0.2%) with status epilepticus, and early seizures were associated with subsequent post-traumatic epilepsy after adjustment for confounders - the cohort-level severity and progression anchor.

references.citation: Kalas M, Miksiewicz M, Kowalke A, Sieminski M. Post-Traumatic Hypopituitarism: A Neglected Consequence of Traumatic Brain Injury. Neuroendocrinology. 2023;113(6):579-588. doi:10.1159/000529327. PMID 36693336.
references.note: Dedicated review of post-traumatic hypopituitarism stating that its prevalence has been significantly underestimated over the past twenty years, that its pathogenesis is heterogeneous, that unrecognized and untreated disease has negative socioeconomic and quality-of-life consequences, and that no clear follow-up or screening algorithm has been established - the condition-definition and neglect anchor.

references.citation: Zaben M, El Ghoul W, Belli A. Post-traumatic head injury pituitary dysfunction. Disabil Rehabil. 2013 Mar;35(6):522-525. doi:10.3109/09638288.2012.697252. PMID 22779906.
references.note: Review recording that the hypophyseal vessels are anatomically vulnerable to shearing injuries, raised intracranial pressure, and anterior skull-base fractures with pituitary ischaemia or haemorrhage common at autopsy, that post-traumatic hypopituitarism can affect all grades of injury severity and is difficult to diagnose because features overlap post-concussive symptoms, and that no screening consensus exists - the mechanism and severity-breadth anchor.

references.citation: Pignata S, Scambia G, Katsaros D, et al. Carboplatin plus paclitaxel once a week versus every 3 weeks in patients with advanced ovarian cancer (MITO-7): a randomised, multicentre, open-label, phase 3 trial. Lancet Oncol. 2014;15(4):396-405. PMID 24582486
references.note: Randomized phase 3 trial of 810 eligible women with ovarian cancer receiving carboplatin plus paclitaxel reported grade 2 or worse neuropathy in 6% of the weekly-treatment group and 17% of the every-three-weeks group. Supports a paclitaxel-containing-treatment complication pathway, not neuropathy attribution from ovarian cancer itself.

references.citation: Pelsma ICMP et al. Quality of care evaluation in non-functioning pituitary adenoma with chiasm compression: visual outcomes and timing of intervention clinical recommendations based on a systematic literature review and cohort study. Pituitary. 2020;23(4):417-429. PMID 32419072
references.note: Systematic review of 44 studies involving 4,789 patients with nonfunctioning pituitary macroadenoma/chiasmal compression evaluated visual dysfunction and outcomes after decompression. Supports an anatomy-specific compressive visual pathway, not visual impairment from every pituitary neoplasm.

references.citation: Humbert M, Kovacs G, Hoeper MM, et al. 2022 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2022;43(38):3618-3731. PMID 36017548
references.note: Multisociety guideline classifies pulmonary hypertension by mechanism, notes that symptoms are linked to right-ventricular dysfunction, and includes dedicated management of advanced right-ventricular failure in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Supports a phenotype-bounded progression pathway, not generic all-PH-to-CHF causation.

references.citation: Garbarino et al., Behavioral Sleep Medicine (2020), PMID 30453780
references.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis found anxiety symptoms common in adults with OSA and described the relationship among OSA, anxiety, and depression as probably bidirectional; supports association, not automatic individual causation.

references.citation: Bandak M, Jørgensen N, Juul A, et al. Testosterone deficiency in testicular cancer survivors - a systematic review and meta-analysis. Andrology. 2016;4(3):382-388. PMID 27009402
references.note: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 12 publications found increased testosterone-deficiency risk after standard chemotherapy (OR 1.8), non-conventional therapy (OR 3.1), and infradiaphragmatic radiotherapy (OR 1.6) compared with testicular germ-cell cancer survivors treated with orchiectomy alone. Supports a treatment-specific hypogonadism pathway, not automatic attribution from the cancer diagnosis itself.

references.citation: Renal and ureteral complications of urethral stenosis, PMID 8571802
references.note: Clinical series of 180 patients with urethral stenosis reporting renal-ureteral complications including ureterohydronephrosis; supports an obstruction-to-upper-tract-dilation pathway but not automatic individual causation.
